identity.title: ALMA's view of the nearest neighbors to the Sun. The submm/mm SEDs of the α Centauri binary and a new source

paper_type_evidence.quote: We used the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) to study the chromospheric emission of the $\alpha$ Centauri binary system in all six available frequency bands during Cycle 2 in 2014-2015.

evidence.quote: Outside the solar system, Alpha Centauri ($\alpha \, {\rm Cen}$) is our nearest neighbour, only a little more than a parsec away ($\pi=\,$0$\stackrel {\prime \prime}{_{\bf \cdot}}$742).

question.value: What are the submm/mm SEDs and chromospheric temperature structures of alpha Cen A and B, and what is a new point source detected in Band 8?

evidence.quote: The comparison of the observed spectral energy distributions with theoretical model computations provides the chromospheric structure in terms of temperature and density above the stellar photosphere
The ALMA program code is 2013.1.00170.S
The binary $\alpha \, {\rm Cen\,A}$B was observed in all six ALMA continuum bands during the period July 2014 to May 2015

findings_qualitative.value: SEDs flatten at long wavelengths, likely optically thin free-free beyond 1.5 mm

evidence.quote: likely because the free-free emission is turning from optically thick to thin beyond 1.5 mm

claims.hypothesis: Do modified solar chromosphere models reproduce alpha Cen submm/mm SEDs?
claims.experiment: Compared Band 3-9 brightness temperatures with modified C7 model
claims.result: T_min/T_eff=0.61 for A; good fit except Band 3
claims.finding: Solar-like non-radiative heating operates in alpha Cen

evidence.quote: This adapted solar model works very well for the solar analog $\alpha \, {\rm Cen\,A}$ (G2 V), but also for the K1 V star $\alpha \, {\rm Cen\,B}$.

claims.experiment: Single Band 8 detection with upper limits elsewhere; solar system object search
claims.result: 4.24 mJy at 740 um; no known object to V=26
claims.finding: Likely a distant solar system object (ETNO), but uncertain

evidence.quote: Unless it is a highly variable background source, we find it most likely that it is a distant member of our solar system.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Companion star, planet at alpha Cen, and Pluto-like body for U rejected

evidence.quote: A companion star of the $\alpha \, {\rm Cen}$ system does not present a viable explanation

limitations_admitted.value: Single epoch, single detection for U

evidence.quote: With only one epoch and only one detection, we are left with little information regarding that object’s nature
